title: The dissent record, its closed severity set, and its blocker tooth
action:
Add `bee cells dissent`, the verb a dispatched worker uses to disagree with the cell it was handed (per 4b7aa303, a2affcba). Write it in a NEW module `verbs/cells/dissent.rs`, declared from `verbs/cells/mod.rs`.

The record carries exactly four author-supplied fields — target, claim, alternative, severity — and appends to the target cell's trace under its own key, never overwriting an existing one. Severity is a CLOSED set: `blocker` and `consider`. Any other value refuses by name and writes nothing, the way every other closed set in this crate refuses.

Three behaviors beyond the plain write, each one a locked requirement:

1. SECRET SCAN the free text. The claim and alternative reach another session's reader, and cell-trace text is unscanned today — verified: `find_secret_pattern` at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/audit.rs:60 has one caller, `assert_safe_decision_fields` at audit.rs:278, which the trace path never reaches, and `run_block` writes its reason straight through. Route the two text fields through the same refusal.
2. RELEASE the writer's claim. A worker that dissents is exiting. `run_block` (packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs:1102) does NOT release, which would leave the claim sitting and force the orchestrator's verdict onto an audited override as its routine path. Release here instead.
3. At `blocker` severity ONLY, block the target cell so its dependents stop being schedulable. Reuse the existing block mutation rather than writing a second one; `run_block` at handlers_close.rs:1102 shows the status write, the reason field, and the `append_attempt` call (packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/trace.rs:88). A `consider` dissent changes no status at all.

Declare the verb everywhere it must be declared, or a contract test passes on an absent row: the module and `verbs/cells/mod.rs`; the cells dispatch table at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/util.rs — the `match verb {` is at util.rs:68, with siblings `"block" => run_block(flags, use_json, t0),` at :74 and `"judge-record" => run_judge_record(flags, use_json, t0),` at :88; the router coverage line at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/router.rs:70, currently `    "cells add|update|claim|unclaim|cap|finish|block|drop|reopen|escalate",`; `src/generated/registry_payload.json`, which is HAND-EDITED — `bee dev regen` never touches it; and the flag ratchet at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/catalog.rs:611, currently `        const PINNED_FLAG_COUNT: usize = 195;`, bumped on purpose with the reason recorded beside it for whichever of target/claim/alternative/severity are genuinely new flag names.

Do NOT touch `bee cells escalate` — a2affcba bans reusing that name, which means model tier.

truths: A worker records a dissent against a cell and the four fields read back off that cell's trace, unchanged.
A severity outside {blocker, consider} refuses by name and leaves the cell file byte-identical.
A blocker dissent leaves the target cell blocked, and a cell that depends on it is no longer schedulable.
A consider dissent leaves the target cell's status untouched.
Claim or alternative text carrying a secret-shaped or control-token string refuses before anything is written.
After a successful record, the writing worker no longer holds the claim on the target cell.
